_comment: Intel Arc B-series specs from published Intel sources. Each row cites the SKU spec page or Intel datasheet. FP16 and BF16 share the same XMX throughput tier on Xe2; we list the value once. INT4 is not separately published by Intel — for W4A8 paths, use the INT8 number (the activation side governs throughput). Die note: B70 uses BMG-G31 (full die, 32 Xe cores, 256-bit bus). B580 and B60 use BMG-G21 (smaller die, 20 Xe cores, 192-bit bus). Compute and bandwidth scale with die. pci_device_id: the value shown in brackets by `xpu-smi discovery` / `lspci -d 8086:` (e.g. `Intel(R) Graphics [0xe223]` → arc-pro-b70). Source: lspci on the hardware for B580 and B70; remaining IDs derived from Linux xe kernel driver (include/drm/intel/pciids.h INTEL_BMG_IDS list).
_framework_factors_comment: Roofline efficiency knobs. MFU = Model FLOP Utilization (compute roof, prefill). BWE = Bandwidth Efficiency (memory roof, decode). Ranges are community-typical for the named runtime, not measurements from any specific stack. Width reflects 'maturing kernel coverage' as the lower bound and 'well-tuned kernel' as the upper. The skill emits a band, not a point estimate. Use scripts/calibrate.py to anchor these to your specific (image, device) combination — it overrides the band for that run.
_quant_comment: Bytes per parameter and which compute tier each quant routes to on Xe2 XMX. W4A8 (awq/gptq/auto-round/inc) uses the INT8 DPAS tier because activations are int8. Plain FP8 weights stay on the FP16/BF16 tier — Battlemage XMX has no native FP8 matmul DPAS, so kernels dequantize FP8 → BF16 before the matmul. FP8 still saves memory bytes (1.0 vs 2.0 per weight) but does not get the int8-tier compute speedup.
